test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: From a taxi stand, two cabs start at a speed of 54 km/hr at an interval of 29 minutes, both cabs travelling in the same direction. A man coming in the opposite direction towards the taxi stand meets the cabs at an interval of 12 minutes. Find the speed (in km/hr) of the man.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by **cab** in (29 − 12) minutes = Distance covered by **man** in 12 minutes.

Ratio of **Speed of Cab** : **Speed of Man** = 12 : (29 − 12) = 12 : 17.

Given, **Speed of Cab** = 54 km/hr (12 units → 54).

1 unit → 54 ÷ 12 = 4.5. Therefore, 17 units → 17 × 4.5 = 76.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 76.5 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76ab5c362c7aaed0ed93f37a50941b6fdeea4c0486b20ffc8d5d55925f3fbc98.png] 

**Given:** **Speed of Cab** = 54 km/hr, **Time Interval of Cabs** = 29 min, **Meeting Interval** = 12 min.

**Formula:** Distance between cabs = Relative Speed × Meeting Time.

⇒ Distance between two cabs = 54 × (29 ÷ 60) km.

⇒ Let **Speed of Man** be 'v' km/hr.

⇒ Relative speed (opposite direction) = (54 + v) km/hr.

⇒ Distance = Relative Speed × Meeting Interval.

⇒ 54 × (29 ÷ 60) = (54 + v) × (12 ÷ 60).

⇒ 54 × 29 = (54 + v) × 12.

⇒ 1566 = 648 + 12v.

⇒ 12v = 1566 − 648 = 918.

⇒ v = 918 ÷ 12 = 76.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 76.5 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their **Relative Speed** is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Distance Constant Concept

The distance between two consecutive vehicles is always **Speed × Time Interval**. This distance is covered at the relative speed by an observer moving in the opposite direction.

Time Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent. To convert **minutes to hours**, divide by 60. To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.</p
